rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s incitement through ignorant deeds and mistreatment can draw the Prophet toward anger and retaliation; the refuge command is addressed to him but intended for his community because he is infallible.
rows.anchor: لو نزغ الشيطان بأعمالهم المبنية على الجهالة وإساءتهم إليك ليسوقك بذلك إلى الغضب والانتقام فاستعذ بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 7:201 explains the preceding command to seek refuge when Satan incites.
rows.anchor: نحو تعليل للأمر في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The satanic visitation may be Satan circling the heart to cast a whisper, or the whisper itself circling until it enters and settles; the senses converge.
rows.anchor: الذي يطوف حول القلب ليلقي إليه الوسوسة أو وسوسته التي تطوف حول القلب لتقع فيه وتستقر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is explanatory on the first interpretation of the visitation and originative on the second.
rows.anchor: و { من } بيانية على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance is reflection that guides a person to a conclusion previously overlooked or unknown.
rows.anchor: والتذكر تفكر من الانسان في أمور لتهديه إلى نتيجة مغفول عنها أو مجهولة قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing remember that God is their Lord who owns and nurtures them; entrusting their affairs to Him defeats Satan’s plot and removes heedlessness.
rows.anchor: تذكروا أن الله هو ربهم الذي يملكهم ويربيهم يرجع إليه أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their restored insight means the veil of heedlessness no longer covers their sight.
rows.anchor: ورفع عنهم حجاب الغفلة فإذا هم مبصرون غير مضروب على أبصارهم بحجاب الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse parallels the assurance that Satan has no authority over believers who rely on God.
rows.anchor: في معنى قوله إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge is remembrance because it recognizes God as the sole support against the attacking enemy; it is also reliance on God.
rows.anchor: الاستعاذة بالله نوع من التذكر لأنها مبنية على أن الله سبحانه وهو ربه هو الركن الوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the brothers seems circumstantial.
rows.anchor: كأن الجملة حالية، والمراد بإخوانهم إخوان المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers are the polytheists’ allied devils, as in the description of spendthrifts as Satan’s brothers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإخوانهم إخوان المشركين وهم الشياطين كما وقع قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqsar means desist or stop; the clause can mean either that devils keep aiding the polytheists or that the polytheists do not desist from error.
rows.anchor: والإقصار الكف والانتهاء. والمعنى أن الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtiba is the iftiʿāl form of jibāya, gathering or collecting.
rows.anchor: الإجتباء افتعال من الجباية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers reject signs when given and, when they are delayed, sarcastically ask why the Prophet did not assemble a sign from here and there.
rows.anchor: كلام منهم جار مجرى التهكم والسخرية والمعنى على ما يعطيه السياق

words: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet replies that he has no control over the matter and follows his Lord’s revelation; the Quran is insight from God, guidance, and mercy for believers.
rows.anchor: ليس لي من الأمر شيء و { إنما اتبع ما يوحى إلي من ربي هذا } القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insat means silence while listening; it is also explained as listening in silence.
rows.anchor: الإنصات السكوت مع استماع، وقيل هو الاستماع مع سكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to listen to the Quran and remain silent.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى استمعوا للقرآن واسكتوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view identifies those who claim to hear but do not hear as the People of the Book, specifically the Jews of Qurayza and Nadir; the author calls it far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل أن المراد بالذين قالوا سمعنا وهم لا يسمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage censures the previously mentioned unbelievers and calls them the worst of all creatures that walk the earth.
rows.anchor: تعريض وذم للذين سبق ذكرهم من الكفار على ما يعطيه سياق الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the deaf, the dumb” refers back to those already mentioned.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن اللام في قوله { الصم البكم } للعهد الذكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are deaf and dumb to truth because they lack the means to receive it: they neither hear nor speak truth.
rows.anchor: لا طريق لهم إلى تلقي الحق لفقدهم السمع والنطق فلا يسمعون ولا ينطقون

words: وَلَوْ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًۭا لَّأَسْمَعَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God found no good in them and did not enable them to hear and accept truth; without readiness, even granting hearing would leave them turning away.
rows.anchor: لم يجد عندهم خيرا ولم يعلم به ولو كان لعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good is a sound inner disposition that establishes readiness to accept truth and settles in the heart.
rows.anchor: المراد بالخير حسن السريرة الذي يثبت به الاستعداد لقبول الحق ويستقر في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If He caused them to hear” assumes they lack settled readiness, so it does not imply that granting hearing would create good in them while they then reject it.
rows.anchor: المراد بقوله { ولو أسمعهم } الإسماع على تقدير عدم الاستعداد الثابت المستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command reinforces the earlier call to obey God and the Messenger and not turn away after hearing the truth.
rows.anchor: إلى إطاعة الدعوة الحقة وعدم التولي عنها بعد استماعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger calls to what gives human beings life by taking them out of ruin; God is nearer than their hearts and they will return to Him, so they should be heedful and resolute.
rows.anchor: هذه الدعوة دعوة إلى ما يحيي الإنسان بإخراجه من مهبط الفناء والبوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is the greatest blessing and highest possession of a living being, who sees only nonexistence beyond it; consciousness and will are sought-after effects of life.
rows.anchor: الحياة أنعم نعمة وأعلى سلعة يعتقدها الموجود الحي لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are equipped to preserve spiritual life, the reality of their existence, just as created kinds are equipped to preserve themselves.
rows.anchor: وقد جهز الإنسان وهو احد الموجودات الحية بما يحفظ به حياته الروحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human faculties identify benefits and warn of harms; innate divine guidance directs humanity toward its happiness, so its original constitution cannot err.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجهاز الإنساني يشخص له خيراته ومنافعه، ويحذره من مواطن الشر والضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People innately apprehend the happiness of their existence without doubt, as created kinds naturally move toward what benefits them; errors come from opposing influences that divert them toward harm.
rows.anchor: كان من الحتم الضروري أن يدرك الإنسان سعادة وجوده إدراكا لا يقع فيه شك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates external misdirection with a heavy body that naturally settles on earth, rises only under an external force, and returns unless an obstacle diverts it.
rows.anchor: كالجسم الثقيل الأرضي الذي يستقر بحسب الطبيعة الأرضية على بسيط الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran teaches that human nature recognizes right belief and action; the author cites primordial disposition, divine creation and guidance, responding to reminders, and purification of the soul.
rows.anchor: فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People stray not because innate and divine guidance leads to ruin, but because they neglect reason, forget guidance, follow desire, and accept what Satan’s forces adorn.
rows.anchor: بل لأنه اغفل عقله ونسي رشده واتبع هوى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following conjecture and desire conflicts with guidance already received from God; the author cites the person who makes desire a god.
rows.anchor: إن يتبعون إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truthful knowledge and action urged by human nature are requirements of happy life; they follow from that life and restore it when opposing influences weaken it.
rows.anchor: فهذه الأمور التي تدعو إليها الفطرة الإنسانية من حق العلم والعمل لوازم الحياة السعيدة الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning from innate and divine guidance means losing beneficial knowledge and righteous action, becoming like the dead through ignorance and impaired will; only true knowledge and action revive a person.
rows.anchor: فقد فقد لوازم الحياة السعيدة من العلم النافع والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in limā yuḥyīkum means “to” (ilā), a common usage.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله { لما يحييكم } بمعنى إلى، وهو شائع في الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger calls to the true religion, Islam, which the Quran explains as following human nature’s call to beneficial knowledge and righteous action.
rows.anchor: والذي يدعو إليه الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هو الدين الحق وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond ordinary worldly life until death, accompanied by awareness and voluntary action, the Quran describes a subtler reality of life.
rows.anchor: وللحياة بحسب ما يراه القرآن الكريم معنى آخر أدق مما نراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world’s life is play and pastime while the Hereafter is true life; worldly preoccupation with illusions veils people from the more important aims of existence and spirit.
rows.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings have a higher afterlife whose veil will be removed; it is free of play, idle talk, and sin, and is traversed by faith’s light and the spirit of servitude.
rows.anchor: فللإنسان حياة أخرى أعلى كعبا وأغلى قيمة من هذه الحياة الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites believers whose hearts hold faith and are strengthened by a spirit from God, and the person who was dead, then given life and light to walk among people.
rows.anchor: أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Holy Spirit and revelation described as a spirit suggest a further life above the two already discussed.
rows.anchor: وأيدناه بروح القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true life nobler and more complete than worldly religious life is attained through readiness formed by religion and entry into the company of the righteous.
rows.anchor: يتلبس بها إذا تم استعداده بالتحلي بحلية الدين والدخول في زمرة الأولياء الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting Islam’s true call brings real life, which also gives rise to Islam, beneficial knowledge, and righteous action.
rows.anchor: فالتلبس بما تندب إليه الدعوة الحقة من الإسلام يجر إلى الإنسان هذه الحياة الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects this life to God’s promise of a good life and reward for a believing man or woman who acts righteously.
rows.anchor: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياه طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is unrestricted: it can cover all the Prophet’s calls that revive hearts, any call embodying life, or their results in true happiness, including life near God in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: والآية أعني قوله فيها { إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم } مطلق لا يأبى الشمول لجميع دعوته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation, tied to the occasion of revelation, identifies the call as jihad, which revives the community’s cause and strengthens its religion.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم إن المراد بقوله { إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم } بالنظر إلى مورد النزول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the call as martyrdom in jihad, since God calls those killed in His way alive with their Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى الشهادة في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The call is also explained as a call to faith, the heart’s life as unbelief is its death, or simply a call to truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى الإيمان، فإنه حياة القلب والكفر موته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the call as the Quran and religious knowledge, since knowledge is life, ignorance death, and the Quran light, life, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى القرآن والعلم في الدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the call as a summons to Paradise because it contains everlasting life and eternal bliss.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى الجنة لما فيها من الحياة الدائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each proposed interpretation can fit, but there is no reason to restrict the verse’s expansive meaning.
rows.anchor: وهذه الوجوه المذكورة يقبل كل واحد منها انطباق الآية عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaylūla is interposition; qalb is the organ and often the Quranic locus of cognition and inward emotions, that is, the human soul acting through inner faculties.
rows.anchor: الحيلولة هي التخلل وسطا، والقلب العضو المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates and governs these faculties, giving or withholding them as He wills.
rows.anchor: يتصرف فيها بإيجادها، ويتصرف فيها بتمليك الإنسان ما شاء منها كيف شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other created things, like humans, have a self and attributes, powers, effects, and actions.
rows.anchor: ونظير الإنسان في ذلك سائر الموجودات فما من شيء في الكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God truly owns every created entity and all its attributes and appendages.
rows.anchor: إلا والله سبحانه هو المالك بحقيقة معنى الكلمة لذاته ولتوابع ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes created things owners of what He grants them; He remains the true owner between them and themselves and their attributes.
rows.anchor: وهو المملك إياه كلا من ذاته وتوابع ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives created beings what He wills and withholds what He wills.
rows.anchor: وإعطائه ما أعطى، وحرمانه ما حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same is true of all created things: God truly owns each entity, its attributes, powers, effects, and actions.
rows.anchor: فما من شيء في الكون وله ذات وتوابع ذات من قوى وآثار وأفعال إلا والله سبحانه هو المالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the intermediary between a person and their heart and is nearer than anything, as the Quran says He is nearer than the jugular vein.
rows.anchor: وهو أقرب إليه من كل شيء كما قال تعالى ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As true owner, God is nearer to a person than their own self and faculties, which He grants and connects to them.
rows.anchor: أقرب إليه حتى من نفسه وقوى نفسه التي يملكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection reveals God’s sole true ownership and nullifies merely apparent ownership and authority.
rows.anchor: فإن الحشر والبعث هو الذي ينجلي عنده أن الملك الحق لله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause warns that God truly owns people and their hearts, is nearer than anything, and will gather them to Himself, when no other power can avail them.
rows.anchor: فكأن الآية تقول واعلموا أن الله هو المالك بالحقيقة لكم ولقلوبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God interposes between each person and their heart and everything they own or are connected to.
rows.anchor: فالله سبحانه هو الحائل المتوسط بين الإنسان وبين قلبه وكل ما يملكه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When truth calls to monotheism, a person must answer: God is manifest truth, no veil can conceal Him, and no doubt or whisper can make one ignorant of His oneness.
rows.anchor: فإذا دعاه داعي الحق إلى كلمة الحق ودين التوحيد الذي يحييه لو استجاب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to the heart than the person is, so He knows its contents better than the person does.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان تعالى أقرب إلى قلب الإنسان منه فهو أعلم بما في قلبه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person must answer truth inwardly as well as verbally, avoiding hypocrisy; God knows the heart and will disclose its contents at resurrection.
rows.anchor: فعلى الإنسان إذا دعاه داعي الحق إلى ما يحييه من الحق أن يستجيب دعاءه بقلبه كما يستجيبه بلسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God owns the heart, its faith, doubt, fear, hope, calm, and anxiety are related to His action through guidance, abandonment, or other divine nurturing.
rows.anchor: فما يجده الإنسان في قلبه من إيمان أو شك أو خوف أو رجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts in the heart as its true owner, according to His will, without being prevented or censured.
rows.anchor: يتصرف بما شاء ويحكم بما أراد من غير أن يمنعه مانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s unanswerable judgment and universal sovereignty support the claim that He alone governs the heart.
rows.anchor: والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must not regard faith, good intentions, or resolve as independently under their control: God truly owns the heart and can turn it from uprightness to deviation.
rows.anchor: فمن الجهل أن يثق الإنسان بما يجد في قلبه من الإيمان بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should commit to truth and good while fearing that God may turn them from happiness to misery, and should not feel secure from His plan.
rows.anchor: فمن الواجب عليه أن يؤمن بالحق ويعزم على الخير على مخافة من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone whose heart resists truth and good should promptly answer God and His Messenger, not surrender to despair, because God can repair the inner state and turn the heart toward what is best.
rows.anchor: عليه أن يبادر إلى استجابة الله ورسوله فيما يدعوه إلى ما يجيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gathers profound divine knowledge: it removes disbelievers’ excuse for ignoring God, confronts hypocrites with God’s knowledge of their hearts, and teaches believers they do not independently own their hearts.
rows.anchor: من أجمع الآيات القرآنية تشتمل على معرفة حقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The teaching removes arrogance in those who imagine independent dominion and keeps them from being deceived by inner piety; it also relieves despair in those overwhelmed by desire and worldly diversions.
rows.anchor: فيزول بذلك رذيلة الكبر عمن يرى لنفسه استقلالا وسلطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s interposition explains the command to answer God and the Messenger under every valid sense of the call to life.
rows.anchor: على جميع التقادير من وجوه معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s meaning is broader than the interpretations reported by other exegetes.
rows.anchor: أن الآية أوسع معنى مما أورده المفسرون من تفسيرها

rows.speaker: من قال
rows.claim: One view says God is nearer to a person than their heart, as in the verse about nearness to the jugular vein, and takes this as a severe warning.
rows.anchor: كقول من قال إن المراد أن الله سبحانه أقرب إلى المرء من قلبه

rows.speaker: من قال
rows.claim: Another view says the heart cannot conceal anything from God, who is nearer to it than the person and knows it before its owner does.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال إن المراد أن القلب لا يستطيع أن يكتم الله حديثا

rows.speaker: من قال
rows.claim: A third view says God comes between a person and benefiting from the heart through death, urging prompt obedience before opportunity is lost.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال إن المراد أنه يحول بين المرء وبين الانتفاع بقلبه بالموت

rows.speaker: من قال
rows.claim: Another view says God changes hearts between states, replacing fear of battle with security by intervening between people and their fearful thoughts.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال معناه أن الله سبحانه يملك تقليب القلوب من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: A report from the Imams of the Prophet’s family says God prevents a person from mistaking truth for falsehood or falsehood for truth; no grading is stated here.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في الحديث عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن المراد بذلك أن الله سبحانه يحول بين الإنسان
